title: Traffic Sculptor: SLO-driven throttles, routing and safe rollback protocol for cost-focused batch/cache tuning
creator: Avery Chen
description: Introduce a runtime component (Traffic Sculptor) that applies SLO-aware rate limiters, selective routing to safer model variants, and anomaly-triggered rollbacks when automated batching/caching recommendations are applied. The goal is to safely realize cost savings from aggressive batch/cache profiles while enforcing latency and throughput SLOs and minimizing customer impact.
acceptance_criteria: Traffic Sculptor enforces per-tenant and per-route p95/p99 latency SLAs via token/req throttles and prevents batch sizes that exceed configured latency budgets.
Automated routing to cheaper/quantized model variants occurs transparently when headroom and SLO checks pass; fallbacks are automatic on SLO violation or anomaly detection.
Config apply includes a staged canary (shadow cohort + traffic slice) and an automated rollback window if latency/FF rate/error thresholds are exceeded.
Operators can view per-apply evaluation metrics in Console: split by cohort, model variant, batch size, KV hit rate, and cost delta estimates.
Synthetic spike tests and real-traffic anomaly detectors trigger the emergency cutoff with <30s median reaction time and documented playbook steps.
Integration tests (CI) simulate 3 failure modes: slow GPU kernels, KV cache mis-hit regressions, and burst QPS spikes; all must result in rollback in CI harness.
discussion: 2025-03-10 Avery Chen: Drafted ticket after spike during COGS test where batch increase saved 12% cost but p99 increased past SLA on tail customers.
2025-03-11 Marco Ruiz: Prototype rate limiter implemented; needs integration with routing policy service. Initial smoke tests show p95 stable but p99 tail increases for long-context requests.
2025-03-12 Product review (Lara Singh): Must expose explicit "panic cutoff" toggle for enterprise tenants. Add admin override to force immediate fallback to golden config.
2025-03-14 Design (Priya Shah): Suggest UI affordances in Console to preview expected cost delta and worst-case latency delta before apply; created mockups in Drive.
2025-03-15 Eng review (Kenji Ito): Raised risk about cascading rollbacks when many tenants rollback simultaneously; propose jittered rollback windows and backoff to avoid thrash.

2025-03-17 Ops (Nadia Park): Added monitoring panels for cohort KPIs and wired alert rules. Two alert thresholds: warning (p95 degradation > 10% over baseline) and critical (p99 > SLA or error rate spike > 3x).
rollout_plan: 1) Merge runtime + routing PRs behind feature flag 'traffic-sculptor' in runtime-1.20.
2) Run CI integration with synthetic spike scenarios; verify rollback behavior in staging.
3) Canary apply on 1% of traffic for non-critical tenants (shadow cohort enabled for 100% traffic visibility).
4) Expand to 10% after 24h if no warning alerts; expand to 30% after 72h with manual check.
5) Full apply to eligible tenants with gradual ramping and continuous monitoring.
6) If critical threshold hit at any stage, trigger automated rollback and escalation to on-call.
playbook: Alert fires: run 'cohort-diagnostics' dashboard and verify cohort's baseline comparison (last 7d).
If p99 > SLA or error rate increased >3x, flip 'panic-cutoff' for that tenant to force immediate drop to conservative batch/cache profile.
If rollback triggers repeatedly, disable automated batching changes for tenant and open SEV review linking PR and metrics.
Notify customers in impacted segment via support template and prepare mitigation notes for CSM.
implementation_notes: Use token-bucket style rate limiter per-tenant with dynamic bucket size derived from p95 target and observed service time distribution.
Routing policy extension: add 'safety_score' to model variants (higher for quantized but slower tail) and prefer variants only when projected latency budget is positive.

Anomaly detector uses hybrid signals: model kernel latency drift, KV hit rate drop, and sudden batch_size change correlation with tail latency; implement ensemble rule in Prometheus + short ML detector in Observability pipeline.
Rollback mechanism must be idempotent and support circuit-breaker semantics with exponential backoff to prevent rollback storms.
notes: This ticket intentionally separates traffic control and cost recommender: the recommender provides suggested profiles, Traffic Sculptor enforces and safely applies them. Focus is on runtime enforcement + quick rollback rather than recommendation quality improvements. Expect follow-up tickets for UI polish and enterprise policy controls.
